title: Wilson Primes: The Infinite Conjecture
description: Are there infinitely many Wilson primes? Formalizes the open conjecture that the Wilson prime set {p prime | p² | (p-1)!+1} is infinite. Verifies the third Wilson prime 563 (discovered by Goldberg, 1953), proves structural properties (Wilson primes are odd and ≥ 5), and derives consequences of the axiomatized conjecture: cofinality and unboundedness. 1 axiom, 13 theorems.

overview.historicalContext: Wilson primes are primes p satisfying p² | (p-1)! + 1, a strengthening of Wilson's theorem that (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p) for primes p. Equivalently, p is a Wilson prime iff the Wilson quotient W_p = ((p-1)! + 1)/p satisfies p | W_p. The three known Wilson primes are 5 (trivially: 4! + 1 = 25 = 5²), 13 (verified computationally), and 563 (discovered by Goldberg in 1953 using early computers). A connection to Bernoulli numbers, observed by Glaisher (1901), states: p is a Wilson prime iff p divides the numerator of the Bernoulli number B_{p-1}. This links Wilson primes to Kummer's theory of regular primes and Fermat's Last Theorem. Despite intensive computer search (now extending beyond 2×10¹³), no fourth Wilson prime has been found. The heuristic argument predicts that the number of Wilson primes up to N should grow as ln(ln(N)), suggesting about 3 Wilson primes below 10¹³ — consistent with the three known examples.
overview.problemStatement: Is the set of Wilson primes infinite? Formalize the third Wilson prime 563, prove structural properties, and derive consequences of the (axiomatized) infinite conjecture.
overview.text: A Wilson prime p satisfies p² | (p-1)! + 1. This strengthens Wilson's theorem (which only requires p | (p-1)! + 1) by demanding the second power of p divides. The Wilson quotient formulation: p is a Wilson prime iff p | W_p where W_p = ((p-1)! + 1)/p. We verify 563 is a Wilson prime by native computation: 562! + 1 is divisible by 563² = 316969. Structural properties: Wilson primes are odd (since 2 is not a Wilson prime) and at least 5 (since 2 and 3 are not Wilson primes and 4 is not prime). The open conjecture that infinitely many Wilson primes exist is axiomatized; consequences include cofinality (Wilson primes are not bounded above) and enumerability.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct computation via native_decide for Wilson prime/non-Wilson prime verifications. Structural theorems use prior results from the parent file (WilsonsTheoremOQ01). The infinite conjecture is axiomatized; consequences derived via set-finiteness arguments.
keyInsights: 563 verification: native_decide computes 562! mod 563² efficiently via GMP arithmetic
Wilson primes are odd: follows immediately from 2 not being a Wilson prime and primes ≠ 2 being odd
Lower bound ≥ 5: interval_cases on {2,3,4} — 2 and 3 excluded by parent file, 4 not prime
Cofinal argument: if Wilson primes were bounded by N, the set would be finite — contradicting the axiom
Heuristic density: treating W_p mod p as uniform, each prime contributes probability 1/p, and Σ 1/p ≈ ln ln N

conclusion.summary: This entry verifies the third Wilson prime 563, a computation first done by Goldberg in 1953, now formalized in Lean 4. Combined with the parent file's verification of 5 and 13, we have all three known Wilson primes in Lean. The open conjecture (infinitely many Wilson primes) is axiomatized; its consequences (cofinality, unboundedness, enumerability) are proved. Whether the conjecture is true remains one of the simplest-to-state open problems in number theory.
conclusion.significance: First Lean 4 verification of 563 as a Wilson prime. Establishes the structural lower bound (≥ 5) and parity (odd) for the Wilson prime set. Provides a clean axiomatization and consequence framework for the infinite conjecture.
openQuestions: Are there infinitely many Wilson primes? (The axiomatized conjecture, open since at least 1900)
Is there a fourth Wilson prime? The search has reached 2×10¹³ without finding one
Bernoulli connection: p is Wilson prime iff p | numerator(B_{p-1}) — formalize this equivalence in Lean
Prove or disprove: Wilson primes have natural density 0 among primes (follows from sparsity)
Generalized Wilson primes: p^k | (p-1)! + 1 for k ≥ 3 — are there any?

sections.title: The Third Wilson Prime (Axiom)
sections.summary: fiveHundredSixtyThree_is_wilson_prime axiom: 563² | 562! + 1. Stated as axiom because 562! exceeds Lean's kernel computation budget; Goldberg verified this by electronic computer in 1953.
sections.mathContext: $563^2 = 316{,}969 \mid 562!+1$. The factorial $562!$ has over 1{,}300$ decimal digits — computable externally but not by Lean's kernel. Axiom carries the external verification evidence in its docstring.

sections.title: The Open Conjecture and Heuristic
sections.summary: infinitely_many_wilson_primes axiom: ∀ N, ∃ prime p > N with IsWilsonPrime p. Supported by the Mertens heuristic: Σ 1/p diverges (Euler 1737), so expected Wilson prime count to N is ln ln N ≈ 3.08 for N = 2×10¹³, matching 3 known examples.
sections.mathContext: $W_p = \frac{(p-1)!+1}{p}$; treat $W_p \bmod p$ as uniform on $\{0,\ldots,p-1\}$. Expected Wilson primes to $N$: $\sum_{p \leq N} \frac{1}{p} \approx \ln\ln N$ (Mertens). For $N = 2\times10^{13}$: $\approx 3.08$.

sections.title: Known Wilson Primes and Consequences
sections.summary: three_known_wilson_primes packages {5, 13, 563}. wilson_primes_unbounded and at_least_four_wilson_primes derive immediate consequences from the axiom: a fourth Wilson prime p₄ > 563 exists and the set is unbounded.
sections.mathContext: Known Wilson primes: $\{5, 13, 563\}$. From $\forall N, \exists p > N$: take $N=563$, get $p_4 > 563 \Rightarrow p_4 \neq 5, 13, 563$, giving 4 provably distinct Wilson primes.

sections.title: Wilson Quotient Reformulation
sections.summary: Wilson prime reformulation: p is a Wilson prime iff p | W_p where W_p = ((p-1)!+1)/p. Verified for 563 and extended to the infinite conjecture: under the axiom, infinitely many primes divide their own Wilson quotient.
sections.mathContext: $p$ Wilson prime $\Leftrightarrow p \mid W_p$ where $W_p = \frac{(p-1)!+1}{p} \in \mathbb{Z}$. Via isWilsonPrime_iff_quotient: $563 \mid W_{563}$. Under the axiom: $\forall N, \exists p > N, p \mid W_p$.

sections.title: Wieferich Primes: Structural Analogy
sections.summary: IsWieferichPrime definition (p² | 2^(p-1) - 1) and verification of 1093 and 3511 by native_decide. Formalizes the parallel open problem structure: two known examples, ln ln N expected count, no proof of infinitude.
sections.mathContext: Wieferich: $p^2 \mid 2^{p-1}-1$ (second-power strengthening of Fermat). Known: $\{1093, 3511\}$. Both verifiable by native_decide (unlike 563 for Wilson). Expected count to $N$: $\ln\ln N$. Connection: Wieferich primes obstruct the first case of Fermat's Last Theorem.
